title: GPU termination handshake and lease reconciliation refactor
creator: Jonas Reed
description:
Summary: Refactor the GPU fleet termination and lease reconciliation paths to remove race conditions, reduce controller-client API churn, and add explicit termination handshakes with the serving runtime. This ticket consolidates three problem areas: (1) capacity planner / allocation leaks when nodes terminate mid-claim, (2) repeated k8s/cloud API calls under high churn that throttle controller loops, and (3) lack of end-to-end telemetry linking a node's lifecycle events to autoscaler decisions.

Scope:
- Introduce a short-lived lease object (controller-managed) for GPU node claims to replace ad-hoc annotation-based ownership; leases will be renew/release only and decouple from kubelet pod states.
- Implement a termination handshake protocol: autoscaler -> node agent -> runtime drain -> KV-cache flush -> confirm termination. Add backoff and retries for transient failures.
- Batch and coalesce cloud API calls for node termination/label updates to reduce API rate usage and lock contention.
- Add correlation IDs to node events and emit new telemetry dimensions (claim_id, lease_id, termination_reason, backend_region, pool_id).
- Upgrade client libraries: client-go -> v0.29.10, google-cloud-go -> latest stable patch to fix rate-limit handling (see dependency notes).
- Add e2e tests that simulate partial failures (agent misses confirmation, cloud API 429) and assert eventual consistency and no double-allocations.

Motivation: We see intermittent capacity accounting drift after node preemption or when the autoscaler races with cloud termination. This causes short-lived over-allocations and increased tail latency for allocation requests. The current code mutates node annotations in multiple places and makes aggressive single-request calls which exacerbate k8s/cloud throttling. A clearer lease+handshake model simplifies reasoning and provides telemetry hooks for alerting and SLOs.

Acceptance criteria:
- New lease mechanism in place with documented state transitions and unit tests.
- Termination handshake implemented; autoscaler will not release capacity until handshake confirmed, or until a configurable timeout with alerting.
- API call count for termination path reduced by at least 60% in synthetic churn tests.
- No regression in allocation latency (95th percentile within 10% of current baseline).
- Telemetry visible in Console: claim_id correlation on per-request traces and new dashboards for lease failures.

Out of scope: full redesign of the autoscaler's allocation algorithm (this is focused on lifecycle consistency), RBAC changes for private deployments (handled in separate ticket).
comments: 2026-02-21 | Jonas Reed: Initial triage and design sketch. Ran a replay of fleet events from last incident; identified ~3 spots where we re-annotate nodes concurrently. Created design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/22456/GPU+Lease+and+Termination+Handshake

2026-02-28 | Aisha Patel: Spike completed. PoC lease controller implemented locally using leader-election-less config and a CRD with ttlSeconds. Observed ~4x fewer API writes in local churn sim. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4982

2026-03-03 | Marcus Liu (reviewer): Code review feedback - prefer exponential backoff with jitter for handshake retries; move cloud batching into a separate service to keep autoscaler loop thin. Filed follow-up ENG-27710 for batching service extraction.

2026-03-07 | Aisha Patel: Addressed review comments, added metrics for lease_renew_attempts and handshake_latency_ms. Wrote unit tests for lease expiry edgecases. Updated PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4982 (updated).

2026-03-10 | SRE Team (comment): Please add an alert that fires when handshake confirmations drop below 99% over 10m window. Added alert recipe to runbook. Link to draft dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/gpu-lease-health

2026-03-12 | Aisha Patel: Integration testing in staging shows reduced double-allocations; however, observed a 20% increase in handshake_latency in one region tied to legacy node-agent versions. Plan: rolling upgrade of node-agent with compatibility flag. Created rollout ticket ENG-27901.
notes: Trade-offs: leases add an extra object to watch which increases controller complexity, but substantially reduces mutation races. We accepted a small increase in handshake latency for correctness; optimizations (agent-side async ACKs, batching) are planned in follow-ups.
